gaps.sentence: 'I've lost my keys,' she admitted. She admitted that she ___ her keys.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: have lost → had lost.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
gaps.hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
gaps.explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
gaps.explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
gaps.explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

gaps.sentence: 'Where do you live?' he asked me. He asked me where I ___.
gaps.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, and present simple backshifts: do you live → I lived.
